blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: RGBA video generation is essential for creating compositable visual assets in filmmaking, game development, and digital content production. However, generating high-quality RGB appearance alongside temporally coherent transparency remains a significant challenge. Existing text-to-RGBA video methods often entangle RGB and alpha distributions and offer limited control over the precise appearance of a target asset. In addition, incorporating image conditioning typically suffers from the emergence-disappearance effects, which fail existing first-frame or first-and-last-frame conditions due to their fully transparent boundary frames. To address these issues, we present Wan-Alpha++, a unified framework that brings controllable RGBA video generation to both text- and image-to-video diffusion backbones through a shared RGBA latent space, extending our conference version Wan-Alpha from the text-conditioned setting to image-conditioned generation with an interior reference frame. Our method first learns shiftable RGB-alpha distributions while preserving the pretrained RGB prior. Specifically, we introduce a transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion objective to produce distinguishable RGBA latent representations, and a transparency-guided mean sampler that shifts the noise distribution to improve transparency generation and enable spatial controllability. Building upon this RGBA generation prior, we introduce temporal phase reparameterization for image-conditioned effect generation. By cyclically transforming a zero-positive-zero alpha pattern into a positive-zero-positive pattern, it relocates visible content to both temporal boundaries, facilitating effective appearance conditioning with limited RGBA data.
blocks.zh: RGBA视频生成对于在电影制作,游戏开发,和数字内容制作中创造可堆叠的视觉资产至关重要. 然而,在暂时保持一贯透明度的同时,形成高质量的保护责任,仍然是一个重大挑战。 现有的文本到RGBA视频方法经常缠绕RGB和α发行,对目标资产的准确外观提供有限的控制. 此外,纳入图像条件通常受到出现 -- -- 消失效应的影响,这些效应由于边界框架完全透明而未能满足现有的第一帧或第一和最后一帧条件。 为了解决这些问题,我们提出Wan-Alpha++,这是一个统一的框架,通过共享的RGBA潜在空间,将可控RGBA视频生成带给文本和图像到视频的传播主干线,把我们的会议版本Wan-Alpha从文本条件设定扩展到图像条件设定生成带内部参考框架. 我们的方法首先学习可转移的RGB-α分布,同时保留预先训练的RGB前. 具体地说,我们引入了一个具有透明度的双向传播目标,以产生可区分的RGBA潜在表示,并引入一个以透明度为指南的平均取样器,以改变噪音分布,从而改进透明度的产生并实现空间可控性。 在先前的RGBA生成的基础上,我们引入了时间相重测,用于图像条件效应生成. 通过周期性地将零正-零正α图案转换为正-零正α图案,将可见内容迁移到两个时间界限上,以有限的RGBA数据来方便有效的外观调节.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: RGBA extends conventional RGB representation with an alpha channel that describes per-pixel transparency, enabling foreground content to be directly composited with arbitrary backgrounds. As a result, RGBA videos are widely used in game development, filmmaking, television production, user-interface design, and other creative workflows. While automatically generating RGBA videos can substantially reduce manual effort, it faces unique challenges beyond standard RGB video generation: the model must jointly synthesize high-quality RGB appearance, spatially accurate transparency, and temporally coherent alpha evolution.
blocks.zh: RGBA将常规的RGB代表扩展为alpha通道,描述每个像素的透明度,使前景内容能够与任意背景直接复合. 因此,RGBA视频被广泛应用于游戏开发,电影制作,电视制作,用户界面设计,以及其他创意工作流程. 虽然自动生成RGBA视频可以大大减少人工努力,但除了标准RGB视频生成之外,它面临着独特的挑战:模型必须联合合成高质量的RGB外观,空间精确透明,以及时间上一致的α进化.

blocks.en: Early text-to-RGBA video generation methods [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] extend RGBA image generation models to video frameworks. A representative strategy combines the 2D RGBA VAE of LayerDiffuse [ 5 ] with pretrained video diffusion models such as AnimateDiff [ 6 ] . However, an image VAE does not explicitly model temporal consistency and tends to entangle RGB and alpha information in the latent space, resulting in degraded appearance, inaccurate transparency, and limited motion. Subsequent approaches improve temporal modeling through dedicated video architectures. TransPixeler [ 7 ] , for example, introduces alpha tokens, duplicates the generation backbone, and employs cross-RGBA attention for information exchange. Nevertheless, architectural interaction alone does not fully resolve the ambiguity between RGB appearance and alpha transparency; it also incurs substantial computational overhead and remains limited in synthesizing semi-transparent effects such as smoke, illumination, water, and translucent materials.
blocks.zh: 早期的文本到RGBA视频生成方法[1,2,3,4]将RGBA图像生成模型扩展到视频框架. 一种代表性策略结合了LetleDiffuse的2D RGBA VAE[5]与AnimateDiff[6]等经过预先训练的视频传播模型. 然而,一个图像VAE并没有明确地模拟时间一致性,倾向于将RGB和α信息缠绕在潜在空间中,导致外观退化,透明度不准确,运动有限. 随后的方法通过专门的视频架构改进了时间建模. TransPixeler [7] 例如,引入α符,复制生成主干,并使用跨RGBA关注来进行信息交流. 尽管如此,仅靠建筑交互并不能完全解决RGB外观和α透明之间的模糊性;它也会引起大量的计算上浮,在合成半透明效应方面仍然受到限制,如烟雾,照明,水,和半透明材料.

blocks.en: To address these text-driven challenges, our preliminary conference work, Wan-Alpha [ 8 ] , explores RGB-alpha distribution learning for text-to-RGBA video generation. Instead of substantially modifying the pre-trained video-generation backbone, it preserves the learned RGB distribution while shifting the alpha distribution in both latent and noise spaces. Through a transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion objective that produces more distinguishable RGBA latent representations, a transparency-guided mean sampler that enhances transparency generation and enables spatial control, and a carefully constructed RGBA video dataset, Wan-Alpha can generate stable transparency without compromising the RGB generation capability of the pretrained model.
blocks.zh: 为了应对这些文本驱动的挑战,我们的初步会议工作Wan-Alpha[8],探索RGB-alpha发行学习,用于文本到RGBA视频生成. 它没有实质性地修改预先训练的视频生成主干线,而是保留了学到的RGB分布,同时在潜伏空间和噪声空间中转移α分布. 通过透明意识双向传播目标,产生更能区分的RGBA潜在表示,透明导引平均采样器,增强透明度生成和空间控制能力,以及精心构建的RGBA视频数据集,万-阿尔法可以产生稳定的透明度,而不损害预训模型的RGB生成能力.

blocks.en:
Nonetheless, text-to-RGBA video generation methods still fall short in achieving precise control over the visual appearance and spatial composition.
An RGBA reference image offers explicit appearance and transparency information, yet directly extending existing image-to-RGB models to RGBA video generation remains a challenging and largely unexplored task.
A fundamental limitation arises from their first-frame or first-and-last-frame conditioning mechanisms [ 9 , 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 ] , which assume that the target content is observable at temporal boundaries of the generated video. This assumption breaks down for RGBA effects, where complete disappearance of content at the first and last frames is a common and often desirable design choice.
A straightforward solution is to directly modify the condition mask to support an interior reference, which requires a large amount of data that is prohibitively expensive to collect.
Alternatively, inference-time gradient guidance may optimize a designated interior frame toward the reference image, but such a soft constraint cannot guarantee exact appearance and alpha preservation and may compromise generation quality.
Consequently, middle-frame-conditioned RGBA video generation faces two coupled challenges: modality adaptation from RGB to RGBA generation and temporal-conditioning adaptation from boundary to interior reference frames.
blocks.zh:
尽管如此,文本到RGBA视频生成方法仍不足以准确控制视觉外观和空间组成。
RGBA的参考图像提供了明确的外观和透明度信息,但将现有的图像到RGB模型直接扩展到RGBA的视频生成仍然是一项具有挑战性且基本未探索的任务.
一个根本的限制来自其第一帧或第一帧或最后一帧的调节机制[9,10,11,12,13],这些机制假设目标内容在生成的视频的时间界限上是可观察到的. 这种假设因RGBA效果而分解,在第一帧和最后一帧完全消失的内容是常见的,往往是可取的设计选择.
一个直截了当的解决方案是直接修改条件遮罩以支持内部参考,这需要大量数据,而收集的数据却过于昂贵。
或者,推论时间梯度指导可以优化指定内框向参考图像的方向,但这种软约束不能保证准确的外观和α保存,并可能损害生成质量。
因此,中期框架条件 RGBA视频生成面临两个相互关联的挑战:从RGB到RGBA生成的模式适应和从边界到内部参考框架的时间调节适应.

blocks.en:
In this paper, we extend our Wan-Alpha [ 8 ] to address the above two challenges, by proposing Wan-Alpha++, a unified framework for controllable text-to-RGBA and data-efficient image-to-RGBA video generation.
Instead of directly modifying the conditioning pattern of the pretrained first-and-last-frame video model, we reparameterize the training distribution through visibility-aware temporal rotation.
Specifically, an RGBA effect that emerges from and subsequently vanishes into transparency is cyclically shifted such that its content-rich interior frames are moved to the temporal boundaries. The resulting sequences contain observable content at both endpoints, allowing us to retain the boundary-conditioning capability of the pretrained model while learning the distinctive temporal evolution of RGBA effects from limited data.
Based on the learned distribution, we introduce transparent-state guidance during inference: the same reference image is supplied at both boundaries, while a user-specified interior interval is guided toward a fully transparent target by minimizing a pixel-space MSE loss along the sampling trajectory.
Unlike an arbitrary RGB target, a fully transparent frame represents a low-complexity state and can therefore be reliably imposed through gradient guidance. Finally, we apply the inverse temporal rotation to recover the desired emergence-disappearance sequence. These two designs are mutually dependent: temporal rotation converts difficult interior conditioning into familiar boundary conditioning, while transparent-state guidance determines the invisible interval required to recover the target temporal pattern.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们扩展了我们的Wan-Alpha[8]以应对上述两个挑战,提出Wan-Alpha++,一个可控文本对RGBA和数据高效图像对RGBA视频生成的统一框架.
我们没有直接修改预先训练的第一帧和最后一帧录像模型的调制模式,而是通过能见度-知时旋转来重新调整训练的分布.
具体来说,从透明度中产生并随后消失的RGBA效应周期性地转移,使其内容丰富的内框转移到时间界限。 由此产生的序列包含两个端点的可观测内容,使我们能够保留预先训练的模型的边界调节能力,同时从有限的数据中了解RGBA效应的独特时间演变.
基于学到的分布,我们在推论中引入了透明状态指导:在两个边界上都提供同样的参考图像,而用户指定的内部间隔则通过在取样轨迹上最小化像素-空间的MSE损失来引导到一个完全透明的目标.
与任意的RGB目标不同,完全透明的帧代表低复杂状态,因此可以通过梯度引导可靠地强制. 最后,我们采用反向时间旋转来恢复所期望的出现-消失序列. 这两个设计是互相依存的:时间旋转将困难的内饰转换成熟悉的边界调节,而透明状态导则决定了恢复目标时间规律所需的无形间隔.

blocks.en: We summarize our major contributions below: • We propose Wan-Alpha, a high-quality text-to-RGBA video generation framework based on shiftable RGB–alpha distribution learning. It enables stable and controllable transparency generation while preserving the RGB synthesis capability of a pretrained video model. • We introduce a transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion objective for distinguishable RGBA latent learning and a transparency-guided mean-shifting strategy for controllable RGBA generation. These designs improve joint RGB-alpha modeling in the latent and noise spaces, respectively. • We construct a high-quality RGBA video dataset containing diverse motion, complex boundaries, and semi-transparent effects. Together with the proposed framework, it enables state-of-the-art performance across generation quality, temporal consistency, transparency rendering, and controllability. • We propose Wan-Alpha++, which extends Wan-Alpha from text conditioning to image conditioning. By introducing temporal phase reparameterization to convert an interior reference into observable boundary conditions, and transparent-state gradient guidance to control the invisible interval and recover the desired emergence-disappearance effect, Wan-Alpha++ achieves middle-frame-conditioned RGBA video generation under limited training data.
blocks.zh: 我们总结我们的主要贡献如下: • 我们提议Wan-Alpha,一个基于可转换的RGB-alpha分布学习的高质量文本到RGBA视频生成框架. 它能够产生稳定和可控制的透明度,同时保持预先训练的视频模型的RGB合成能力。 我们引入了一个具有透明度的双向传播目标,用于可区分的 " GBA " 潜在学习,以及透明指导的 " 平均转移 " 战略,用于可控制的 " GBA " 生成。 这些设计分别改进了潜在空间和噪音空间的RGB-α联合模型。 我们构建了一个高质量的RGBA视频数据集,包含不同的运动,复杂的边界,以及半透明的效果. 它与拟议的框架一起,使一代人之间最先进的性能、时间的一致性、透明度的提高和可控制性得以实现。 我们提出Wan-Alpha++,将Wan-Alpha从文本调制扩展至图像调制. Wan-Alpha++通过引入时间相重测,将内部参考物转化为可观察到的边界条件,以及透明状态梯度引导来控制隐形间隔并恢复所期望的出现-消失效应,在有限的培训数据下实现了中框条件的RGBA视频生成.

blocks.en: We propose Wan-Alpha, a high-quality text-to-RGBA video generation framework based on shiftable RGB–alpha distribution learning. It enables stable and controllable transparency generation while preserving the RGB synthesis capability of a pretrained video model.
blocks.zh: 我们提议Wan-Alpha,一个基于可转换的RGB-alpha发行学习的高质量文本到RGBA视频生成框架. 它能够产生稳定和可控的透明度,同时保留预先训练的视频模型的RGB合成能力.

By introducing temporal phase reparameterization to convert an interior reference into observable boundary conditions, and transparent-state gradient guidance to control the invisible interval and recover the desired emergence-disappearance effect, Wan-Alpha++ achieves middle-frame-conditioned RGBA video generation under limited training data.

blocks.en: II Related work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A RGBA Image Generation
blocks.zh: II- A RGBA 图像生成

blocks.en: Compared with RGB images [ 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 , 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 ] , high-quality RGBA images are substantially more difficult to acquire, making it expensive to train large-scale RGBA generative models from scratch. Existing approaches therefore commonly adapt pretrained RGB image models to transparency generation. LayerDiffuse [ 5 ] introduces latent transparency by adapting the VAE of Stable Diffusion [ 22 ] to encode RGB and alpha information within a shared latent space, followed by parameter-efficient diffusion fine-tuning. AlphaVAE [ 23 ] improves the RGBA representation and substantially reduces the amount of training data required for VAE adaptation. In contrast, Alfie [ 24 ] extracts transparency from the attention features of a pretrained diffusion model without additional training, but mainly supports transparent backgrounds and has limited ability to represent semi-transparent content. Subsequent studies extend RGBA generation to multi-layer image synthesis [ 25 , 26 , 27 , 28 ] and transparent image inpainting [ 29 ] .
blocks.zh: 与RGB图像[14,15,16,17,18,19,20,21]相比,高质量的RGBA图像要获得的难度要大得多,使得从零开始培训大型RGBA基因模型的费用昂贵. 因此,现有方法通常将经过预先培训的RGB图像模型用于提高透明度。 TyleDiffuse [5] 引入了潜在的透明性,将稳定扩散的VAE [22] 用于在共享的潜在空间内编码RGB和α信息,然后进行参数高效扩散微调. AlphaVAE [23] 改进了RGBA的表述,并大大减少了VAE适应所需的培训数据量. 相比之下,Alfie [24] 从未经额外培训的预训传播模式的注意特征中提取透明度,但主要支持透明背景,且代表半透明内容的能力有限. 随后的研究将RGBA生成扩展到多层图像合成[25,26,27,28]和透明图像涂装[29].

blocks.en: Although these methods demonstrate the potential of pretrained RGB priors for transparency generation, they operate on individual images and do not explicitly model temporal alpha evolution.
blocks.zh: 虽然这些方法证明了预先训练的RGB前科对于透明生成的潜力,但它们在单个图像上运行,并且没有明确模拟时间α进化.

blocks.en: II-B RGBA Video Generation
blocks.zh: II-B RGBA 视频生成

blocks.en: RGBA video generation additionally requires temporally coherent motion and transparency, while suitable training data remain scarce. Early approaches [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] combine the image-based LayerDiffuse VAE [ 5 ] with video generation frameworks such as AnimateDiff [ 6 ] , but the lack of explicit temporal modeling in the image VAE often results in unstable alpha channels and limited motion. Other studies develop dedicated architectures for transparent or layered video generation. LayerFlow [ 30 ] formulates layer-aware video synthesis within a unified generation framework, while TransPixeler [ 7 ] duplicates the video backbone and introduces cross-RGBA attention to exchange information between RGB and alpha branches.
blocks.zh: 广播电视协会的录像制作还需要时间上一致的动作和透明度,而适当的培训数据仍然很少。 早期的方法[1,2,3,4]将基于图像的LayerDiffuse VAE[5]与AnimateDiff[6]等视频生成框架结合,但图像VAE中缺乏明确的时间模型往往导致α通道不稳定和运动有限. 其他研究为透明或分层的视频生成开发专用架构. TransPixeler[7]重复了视频主干线,并引入了跨RGBA关注,在RGB和α分支之间交换信息.

blocks.en:
However, these methods either incur substantial computational overhead or remain limited in distinguishing the distribution of RGB appearance from that of transparency. Our preliminary conference work Wan-Alpha [ 8 ] learns shiftable RGB–alpha distributions in the latent and noise spaces, enabling stable and controllable text-to-RGBA video generation while preserving the RGB synthesis capability of the pretrained model. Despite being able to
generate high-quality and diverse videos, text-to-RGBA video generators typically offer less satisfactory spatial controllability ( e.g. , animating the appearance and alpha structure of a user-provided asset).
blocks.zh:
然而,这些方法要么造成大量的计算间接费用,要么在区分RGB外观的分布和透明度方面仍然有限。 我们的初步会议工作是Wan-Alpha[8] 在潜伏和噪音空间学习可转移的 RGB-alpha 分布,从而能够稳定且可控的文本到 RGBA 视频生成,同时保留预训模型的 RGB 合成能力. 虽然可以
生成高质量和多样的视频,文本到RGBA视频生成器通常提供不太令人满意的空间可控性(例如动画用户提供资产的外观和α结构)。

blocks.en: II-C Image-to-RGB Video Generation
blocks.zh: II-C 图像对RGB 视频生成

blocks.en: We review related Image-to-RGB video generation methods, as Wan-Alpha++ is the first Image-to-RGBA video generation model.
blocks.zh: 我们审查相关的图像到RGB视频生成方法,因为Wan-Alpha++是第一个图像到RGBA视频生成模型.

blocks.en:
Boundary-Frame-Conditioned Generation Recent image-to-video generation (I2V) methods generally use reference image(s) to constrain visual appearance while synthesizing
temporal dynamics. A common paradigm places the reference at the first frame. Stable Video Diffusion [ 31 ] adapts
latent video diffusion models to animate a given image.
DynamiCrafter [ 32 ] incorporates both latent-level image features and pixel-level image information into a pretrained text-to-video model. CogVideoX-I2V [ 11 ] encodes the input image with a 3D VAE, pads its latent representation along the temporal dimension, and concatenates it with the noisy video latent. Wan [ 9 ] further scales this paradigm to large diffusion transformers. FrameBridge [ 33 ] reformulates I2V
as a data-to-data bridge process, treating the input image as the starting point of generation instead of an auxiliary condition.
blocks.zh:
边界-Frame-Contitioned Generation 最近的图像到视频生成(I2V)方法一般在合成时使用参考图像来约束视觉外观.
时间动态. 一个共同的范式将参考置于第一个框架. 稳定视频传播 [31] 适应
潜在的视频传播模型来激活给定的图像.
DynamiCrrafter [32] 将潜在水平的图像特性和像素水平的图像信息都整合到一个预先训练的文本到视频模型中. CogVideoX-I2V [11] 将输入图像编码为3D VAE, 沿时间维度铺设其潜伏的表示, 并用吵闹的视频潜伏使其凝固. Wan[9]将这个范式进一步放大到大型扩散变压器. 框架桥 [33] 重构 I2V
作为一种数据对数据桥的过程,将输入图像作为生成的起点而不是辅助条件.

blocks.en: Another line of work incorporates both first- and last-frame conditions to constrain video endpoints. PixelDance [ 34 ] uses a strict first-frame condition together with an optional last-frame instruction to generate motion-rich videos. SEINE [ 35 ] adopts random-mask training and supports first-and-last-frame transition as one of several frame-completion configurations. ToonCrafter [ 36 ] specializes in dual-frame conditioning for generative cartoon interpolation, while ViBiDSampler [ 37 ] performs training-free bidirectional sampling by alternately conditioning forward and backward generation on the two endpoints. Wan2.1-FLF2V [ 9 ] directly trains a large video model with first-and-last-frame conditions.
blocks.zh: 另一条工作线既包括第一段,也包括最后一段,以限制视频终点。 PixelDance [34] 使用严格的第一帧条件和可选的最后帧指令生成运动丰富的视频. SEINE [35] 采用随机任务训练,并支持第一和最后一帧过渡,作为若干帧完成配置之一. ToonCrafter [36] 专门进行基因卡通插图的双帧配置,而ViBiDSampler [37] 通过在两个端点上交替调节前向和后向一代来进行无训练双向取样. Wan2.1-FLF2V [9] 直接列车具有首末帧条件的大型视频模型.

blocks.en: These methods demonstrate the effectiveness of boundary images for appearance and endpoint control. However, their conditioning mechanisms are tied to predefined temporal positions and are unsuitable when the informative reference corresponds to an interior frame, as frequently occurs in emergence–disappearance RGBA effects.
blocks.zh: 这些方法证明了边界图像对外观和端点控制的有效性. 然而,它们的调节机制与预先确定的时间位置有关,当信息参考与内部框架相对应时是不合适的,如出现-消失的RGBA效应中经常出现的情况。

blocks.en:
Training-Free Guidance for Video Generation Training-free diffusion guidance provides an alternative by controlling pretrained models without fine-tuning on specific tasks.
FreeDoM [ 38 ] and MPGD [ 39 ] construct differentiable objectives to guide diffusion sampling while preserving the pretrained generative prior. Recent studies extend this paradigm to video generation. Specifically, MOFT [ 40 ] extracts motion-aware features from video diffusion models and optimizes noisy latents using feature-correlation losses for training-free motion control. TITAN-Guide [ 41 ] further introduces memory-efficient forward-gradient optimization for text-to-video diffusion models and demonstrates its applicability to frame interpolation. FlexTI2V [ 42 ] supports visual conditions at arbitrary temporal positions through dynamic latent-patch exchange, although it does not explicitly use gradient guidance.
blocks.zh:
免费视频生成培训指导提供了一种替代方法,即控制预先培训过的模型,而不对具体任务进行微调。
FreeDOM [38] 和 MPGD [39] 构筑不同的目标,以指导扩散取样,同时保留事先受过训练的基因。 最近的研究将这种范式扩展到视频生成. 具体地说,MOFT[40]从视频传播模型中提取了运动感知特性,并利用特性-脉冲损失来优化无训练运动控制的噪音潜伏. TITAN-Guide [41] 进一步引入了文本到视频传播模型的内存高效前向升级优化,并展示了其适用于帧插值. FlexTI2V [42] 通过动态潜射交换支持任意时间位置的视觉条件,虽然它没有明确使用梯度引导.

blocks.en: These approaches improve conditioning flexibility without model retraining, but generally impose soft sampling-time constraints and cannot guarantee exact reproduction of a target frame.
blocks.zh: 这些方法在没有模式再培训的情况下提高了调节灵活性,但一般会施加软抽样时间限制,无法保证目标框架的确切复制。

blocks.en: III-A Overview
blocks.zh: 三. 概览

blocks.en:
Wan-Alpha++ aims to generate an RGBA video from a user-provided RGBA image while faithfully preserving its appearance and enabling
controllable emergence and
disappearance process.
Building upon our preliminary text-to-RGBA video generation framework [ 8 ] , Wan-Alpha++ substantially advances the previous version and
learns distinguishable RGB-alpha representations and controllable transparency distributions. We first revisit the RGBA VAE training architecture in Sec. 3.2, separating RGB and alpha information in a
latent space. Based on this RGBA representation prior, we construct an image-conditioned model in Sec. 3.3. We first learn a controllable spatial distribution by introducing a transparency-guided sampler. Directly learning middle-frame conditioning requires adapting the pretrained
image-to-video model to a temporal conditioning pattern unseen during
pretraining, which typically demands substantial training data. This is
particularly costly for RGBA video generation because high-quality RGBA videos
are scarce and expensive to collect. We instead reparameterize the temporal phase of RGBA effects, converting a sequence whose informative content lies in the interior into one with observable boundary frames.
This allows the model to retain the pretrained first-and-last-frame conditioning mechanism. During inference, transparent-state guidance determines an interior invisible interval, after which an inverse temporal transformation recovers the desired emergence-disappearance effect. In Sec. 3.4, we introduce the construction of our RGBA dataset for VAE and DiT. All components enable our Wan-Alpha++ to achieve state-of-the-art performance across multiple metrics.

Ablation Study of RGBA Representation Learning We evaluate VAE reconstruction quality using PSNR, SSIM [ 62 ] , and LPIPS [ 63 ] , latent-distribution separation using RGB-Dist and Alpha-Dist, and text-to-RGBA video generation by disabling various components of RGBA representation learning. Specifically, RGB-Dist and Alpha-Dist measure the Euclidean distances (Dist) [ 64 ] between the adapted and pretrained representations for RGB and alpha content, respectively. An effective representation should minimize RGB-Dist while maximizing Alpha-Dist, preserving the pretrained RGB distribution while shifting the alpha distribution.
As shown in Table III , incorporating rendering-based preprocessing and supervision (Rendering) brings significant performance gain in both RGB and alpha reconstruction (see the second row of Table III ), but failing to preserve the pretrained RGB distribution. We further enable transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion (TABD), yielding enhance performance across all evaluation metrics. Our Wan-Alpha incorporates Rendering, TABD, and transparency-guided mean sampler (MS), which further improves text alignment, aesthetics, motion smoothness, and temporal stability without affecting VAE reconstruction quality.

blocks.en:
Image-to-RGBA video generation remains largely unexplored. To the best of our
knowledge, no existing method directly animates a user-provided RGBA asset while
jointly generating its RGB appearance and temporally coherent alpha channel. Therefore, we construct two-stage baselines by integrating Wan2.1-I2V with MatAnyone for normal first-frame-conditioned RGBA video generation, and Wan2.1-FLF2V with MatAnyone for emergence–disappearance RGBA effect video generation, where arbitrary-frame conditioning enables alpha propagation from designated visible reference frames.
The latter is more challenging because the foreground becomes fully transparent during the sequence, requiring the model to synthesize a complete transition between visible and transparent states while preserving the reference appearance. For both normal and RGBA effect video generation, we compare our direct RGBA video generation models against the corresponding two-stage generation baselines in terms of reference fidelity and overall video generation quality.

blocks.en:
We present qualitative comparisons for normal RGBA video generation in Fig. 12 . Two-stage baseline, Wan+MatAnyone, first uses Wan2.1-I2V to render the asset into an RGB video, where transparency information is irreversibly mixed with the composited background. MatAnyone then relies on an interactively specified segmentation mask to initialize the matting process. This two-stage pipeline inevitably introduces and accumulates errors, particularly around thin structures and low-opacity boundaries. These errors are subsequently propagated to the estimated alpha channel, resulting in overly opaque regions or the loss of soft transparency gradients. In contrast, our proposed model achieves superior reference fidelity by jointly modeling RGB appearance and alpha boundaries throughout the video generation process.
More fundamentally, post-hoc matting cannot reliably recover intrinsic transparency once semi-transparent foreground colors have been blended with the background in the generated RGB frames.
It therefore tends to produce nearly opaque alpha values or lose soft transparency gradients.
Beyond these quality limitations, the two-stage pipeline requires separate RGB generation, interactive mask specification, and video matting, making the overall process cumbersome and labor-intensive for practical applications.
In contrast, our method directly generates RGB and alpha channels from the input RGBA asset, eliminating the need for additional user interaction.

blocks.en: Comparison with RGBA Effect Video Generation Baselines We present quantitative comparisons with the competing baseline in Table IV and qualitative comparisons in Fig. 13 . Our proposed framework achieves significant improvements in both DINO-I and CLIP-I over the two-stage Wan2.1-FLF2V+MatAnyone baseline. These performance gains demonstrate that temporal phase reparameterization effectively utilizes the visible conditioning frame to anchor both the structural identity and semantic appearance of the generated effect. Furthermore, our framework consistently achieves superior overall video quality in terms of aesthetic quality, motion smoothness, and temporal flickering. This demonstrates that explicitly learning the transition between visible and transparent states produces more natural content and more temporally coherent alpha evolution than propagating an interactively specified mask after RGB video generation.
blocks.zh: 与 RGBA 效果视频生成基线比较 我们提出了与表四中相互竞争的基准的定量比较和图13中的质量比较。 我们拟议的框架在DINO-I和CLIP-I两个阶段的Wan2.1-FLF2V+MatAnyone基线上都取得了重大改进。 这些性能提高表明,时间相重定时有效利用可见的调节框架,将生成效应的结构特征和语义外观固定起来。 此外,我们的框架在美学质量、运动光滑度和时间闪烁方面始终实现了更高的整体视频质量。 这表明,明确学习可见状态与透明状态之间的过渡,会产生比在RGB视频生成后传播互动指定面具更自然的内容和时间上更一致的α进化.

blocks.en: Fig. 13 further reveals the limitations of applying post-hoc video matting to emergence–disappearance effects. This limitation becomes more pronounced for emergence–disappearance RGBA effect video generation. Although MatAnyone supports arbitrary-frame mask conditioning, it primarily propagates foreground masks and does not explicitly model the transition between positive- and zero-alpha states. Therefore, it tends to leave residual alpha during disappearance or produce temporally unstable boundaries during reappearance.
blocks.zh: 图13进一步揭示了将后热视频配乐应用于出现-消失效应的局限性。 这种限制在出现-消失的RGBA效果视频生成中变得更加明显. 虽然MatAnyone支持任意的帧面罩调制,但它主要传播前缘面罩,并且没有明确模拟正α状态和零α状态之间的过渡. 因此,它往往在消失时留下残余的α,或在重新出现时产生时间不稳定的边界。

blocks.en: We investigate two possible initialization positions for the two-stage Wan2.1-FLF2V+MatAnyone pipeline. When MatAnyone is initialized from the first frame ( First ), its interactive mask can provide a complete foreground at the initial frame. However, requiring the first frame to remain visible is inherently conflicted with the desired emergence-disappearance RGBA effect, in which the content is expected to emerge from a transparent state. Therefore, this setting cannot produce the complete transparent-visible-transparent results. Moreover, errors introduced during RGB video generation (see distorted text shown in Fig. 13 ), are propagated to the subsequent matting stage and cannot be effectively corrected afterward.
blocks.zh: 我们调查两个可能的启动位置 两阶段的Wan2.1-FLF2V+MatAnyone管道。 当MatAnyone从第一个帧(First )初始化后,其交互式面具可以在初始帧提供完整的前缘. 然而,要求第一个框架保持可见性与预期的出现-消失的RGBA效应存在内在冲突,在这种效应中,内容预计将从透明状态中产生. 因此,这种设置不能产生完全透明、可见和透明的结果。 此外,RGB视频生成过程中引入的错误(参见图13所示的扭曲文本),被传播到后续的交配阶段,之后无法有效纠正.

An alternative is to initialize MatAnyone from a visible middle frame ( Middle ). Although the interactive mask successfully extracts the object
at the condition frame, MatAnyone performs forward propagation from this initialization frame. Therefore, the frames preceding the middle condition are discarded, yielding only an incomplete second half of the RGBA video. Moreover, when the object subsequently disappears from the RGB frames, the propagated matting memory continues to predict a foreground region, resulting in a persistent object-shaped artifact in the alpha channel. This limitation highlights that tracking-oriented video matting does not explicitly model transitions to a fully transparent state.

Sensitivity to Guidance Hyperparameters We change the guidance step size and the number of guided sampling steps to examine their effects on video generation performance, with the results reported in Table VII . A larger step size (e.g., η s = 50 \eta_{s}=50 ) provides stronger control over the transparent state, leading to consistent improvements across all metrics. However, an excessively large step size (e.g., η s = 75 \eta_{s}=75 ) overly perturbs the generated appearance, resulting in degraded performance.
For the guidance duration, applying the guidance step for 16 16 or 24 24 slightly improves reference fidelity in terms of DINO-I and CLIP-I, but results in less stable temporal RGBA video effects. Extending guidance to the first 32 32 of 40 40 sampling steps achieves the best overall video generation performance across aesthetic quality, motion smoothness, and temporal consistency. However, applying guidance throughout all 40 40 steps introduces excessive cumulative latent updates, degrading details in visible frames. blocks.en: V Conclusion
blocks.zh: 五 结论

blocks.en:
In this work, we present Wan-Alpha++, a unified framework for high-quality
and controllable RGBA video generation. We first address the entanglement
between RGB appearance and alpha transparency by learning shiftable RGB–alpha
distributions in both latent and noise spaces. The proposed
transparency-aware bidirectional diffusion objective preserves the pretrained
RGB distribution while making alpha representations more distinguishable, and
the transparency-guided mean sampler improves transparency synthesis while
providing coarse spatial control over the generated content.
We further extend RGBA video generation from text conditioning to practical
image conditioning. For emergence-disappearance effects, fully transparent
boundary frames invalidate conventional image-to-video conditioning. Temporal
phase reparameterization addresses this problem by moving visible interior
content to the temporal boundaries, allowing the appearance-conditioning prior
of a pretrained FLF2V model to be reused with limited RGBA data.
Transparent-state guidance subsequently controls the location and duration of
the invisible interval, and inverse phase transformation restores the desired
emergence-disappearance process. Together, these designs provide complementary
spatial and temporal control over RGBA generation.
Experiments demonstrate that Wan-Alpha++ improves RGB quality, reference
fidelity, transparency rendering, motion smoothness, and temporal consistency
over existing RGBA generation and two-stage video-matting pipelines. The
generated assets can be directly composited onto arbitrary backgrounds,
supporting applications in visual effects, filmmaking, game development, and
digital content creation. Future work may extend the proposed temporal
reparameterization to more complex multi-stage transparency events and reduce
the additional inference cost introduced by gradient guidance.
